newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexican daily port, shipping update for Dec 17.
newsitem.headline: Mexican daily port, shipping update for Dec 17.

text.p: Mexico crude port Dos Bocas in Tabasco state remained shut to petroleum exports on Tuesday along with two other major ports as of 1000 local/1600 GMT, the Communications and Transport Ministry said in a daily update.

Two ports in Tabasco state were closed because of wind speeds that registered 55 to 60 km per hour in Dos Bocas and 45 to 50 km per hour in Frontera. La Paz in Baja California was shut amid northwest winds between 55 to 60 km per hour.
Tamaulipas ports Altamira, Tampico and Tuxpan reopened as a cold front in the Gulf of Mexico moved southeast.

Smaller ships were prohibited from sailing at Veracruz, Tampico, Tuxpan, Ciudad del Carmen, Coatzacoalcos and Salina Cruz. A warning was issued for sailing in the southern Gulf of Mexico because of winds and high waves.
The ministry updated port conditions and shipping warnings for the Gulf of Mexico, Caribbean and Pacific Coast.
Slightly cloudy with northwest winds of 10 to 15 knots (19 to 28 kms/11 to 17 miles per hour) with waves reaching three to five feet high.
In the Gulf of Tehuantepec north and northeast winds were clocked at 15 to 20 knots (28 to 38 kms/17 to 22 miles per hour) with wave heights at five to seven feet.

Weak cold front heading south-southwest along the Gulf of Mexico at a speed of 10 km/6 miles per hour and sending showers along the coast of Tamaulipas and Veracruz, with winds from the north at 10 and 15 knots with waves of five to seven feet high.
Rains and wind gusts along the coast of Panama. Dominant winds from the east and northeast causing waves of three to five feet high.
